newsitem.title: UK: Independent Insurance says 1997 started well.
newsitem.headline: Independent Insurance says 1997 started well.

text.p: Independent Insurance Group Plc said on Thursday it had made a good start to the year and would continue to pursue opportunities to expand by acquisition at home and abroad.

Speaking at the company's annual meeting, chairman Garth Ramsay said that the current year had "generally started very well" particularly in the levels of new business and the reduction in loss ratios being experienced.

"Whilst the standard motor and home insurance markets remain competitive, we are seeing signs of a levelling in commercial premium rates and increases in those for employers' liability and contractors risks," said Ramsay.
The company's initiative of offering insurance policies with a term of three or five years was proving to be particularly attractive to commercial insurance buyers, he said.

The roll-out of the firm's workflow and image processing system was continuing and the indications were that real increases in productivity and improved service standards would be rapidly obtained, Ramsay told the meeting.
Shares in Independent Insurance were trading 47 pence higher at 799-1/2 by early afternoon helped by news of an earlier increase in profit forecasts from SBC Warburg.
Dealers said Warburg had repeated its "buy" recommendation and targeted a 10 stg level for the stock.
Analysts at the brokerage declined to comment.
